record.hypothesis: Reparameterize the shared item embedding table so each nonpadding row has unit L2 norm whenever used for either history input or target lookup; padding remains exactly zero. Retain the existing embedding width, GRU topology and dot-product scorer. Removing item-vector magnitude as a popularity shortcut may improve discrimination through embedding direction. Keep features, history policy, loss and optimizer fixed, and reproduce this parameterization in the predictor writer with matching checkpoint shapes.

+class UnitNormItemEmbedding(nn.Embedding):
+    def forward(self, indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        embeddings = super().forward(indices)
+        embeddings = torch.nn.functional.normalize(embeddings, p=2, dim=-1, eps=1e-12)
+        return embeddings.masked_fill(indices.eq(0).unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)

category_rationales.rationale: Normalize the shared item embeddings on every history and target lookup, keeping padding exactly zero. This tests whether embedding direction improves discrimination without item magnitude. Width, GRU topology, dot-product scoring, loss and optimizer stay fixed. Checkpoint shapes remain unchanged; the generated predictor dynamically imports the updated model class.
